title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten distinct study settings inside Kalamazoo College’s Upjohn Library Commons, selected for documented seating, equipment, noise conditions, or collaboration affordances.

cards.title: Set Up for a Working Session
cards.subtitle: Group and individual tables on Upjohn Library Commons Floor 1
cards.notes: Choose an individual or group table, then use the nearby Writing Center, reference offices, or tech desks when the assignment needs support.
cards.short_summary: Flexible tables put academic and technical help within easy reach.
cards.evidence_claim: The first-floor Learning Commons has group and individual study tables near the Writing Center, reference librarians, and computing support desks.
cards.access_notes: Use during Upjohn Library Commons access hours. The first floor can be loud; computers and printers are restricted to Kalamazoo College students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Read Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Café seating in the Upjohn Library Commons lobby
cards.notes: Bring reading or lighter coursework to the lobby seating; choose another floor when your task requires a reliably quiet environment.
cards.short_summary: A social lobby setting suited to reading and less noise-sensitive work.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College identifies the Book Club Café in the Upjohn Library Commons lobby as an area used for socializing and studying.
cards.source_title: About the Library – Library | Kalamazoo College
cards.access_notes: Located in the library lobby and available during building access hours. The first floor is generally not quiet; purchasing café items is not stated as an access requirement.

cards.entity_name: Eugene and Mildred Hoff Yehle Reading Room
cards.title: Work Beside the Fireplaces
cards.subtitle: Usually-quiet reading room on Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2
cards.notes: Use the tables or comfortable seating for reflective work, and keep the solid wood doors open as required by the room-use policy.
cards.short_summary: A usually-quiet room with tables, soft seating, and fireplaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The second-floor Reading Room provides tables, comfortable seating, and fireplaces; library policy designates it for reflective study by students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Available during library access hours. The Reading Room is usually quiet and intended for informal academic use; its solid wood doors must remain open.

cards.title: Pair a Carrel with a Computer
cards.subtitle: Individual computer carrels on Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2
cards.notes: Settle into a computer-equipped carrel for focused digital work; a printer and scanner are also available elsewhere on the same floor.
cards.short_summary: Individual carrels support computer-based research and production.
cards.evidence_claim: Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2 contains study carrels with computers, plus a printer and computers with a scanner near the central staircase.
cards.access_notes: Use during library access hours. Library computers and printers are limited to Kalamazoo College students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Take a Window-Side Carrel
cards.subtitle: Individual carrels on the north side of Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2
cards.notes: Pick an individual window-side carrel for independent work, or shift to a nearby group table when the assignment becomes collaborative.
cards.short_summary: Window-side individual carrels offer a defined place for solo work.
cards.evidence_claim: The north side of Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2 has individual study carrels and group study tables near windows.
cards.access_notes: Available during library access hours. The main second-floor space has a generally medium noise level rather than a quiet-floor designation.

cards.title: Close Out Distractions
cards.subtitle: Single-user sound-isolating booth on Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2
cards.notes: Book a two-hour block for private study or calls, or use the booth without a booking while staying ready to yield to the reservation holder.
cards.short_summary: A single-user booth adds sound dampening, a desk, power, and ventilation.
cards.evidence_claim: Individual Quiet Booth #3 is a sound-isolating single-user room with a seat, sit-or-stand desk, electrical outlets, and a ventilation fan.
cards.access_notes: Students may request a two-hour booking through Media Services. Unreserved use is first come, first served, but users must vacate for a reservation holder.

cards.title: Keep Group Work Contained
cards.subtitle: Four-person sound-isolating booths on Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2
cards.notes: Bring a group of no more than four and reserve a two-hour block when timing matters; the booths sit near study rooms 232–235.
cards.short_summary: Compact group booths support conversation with less spillover into the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Group Quiet Booths #4 and #5 are accessible sound-isolating rooms behind the compact shelving, each seating no more than four people.
cards.access_notes: Students may request a two-hour booking through Media Services. Otherwise, booths are first come, first served and must be yielded to reservation holders.

cards.title: Claim a Defined Study Room
cards.subtitle: First-come study room on Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2
cards.notes: Check room 211 on the north side when you need an enclosed setting, and keep a nearby table or carrel in mind if it is occupied.
cards.short_summary: A designated second-floor room for focused or shared study.
cards.evidence_claim: Kalamazoo College lists ULC 211 as a second-floor study room available to students on a first-come, first-served basis during library hours.
cards.access_notes: Available to Kalamazoo College students first come, first served during library hours; the official page does not provide a reservation option or capacity.

cards.title: Use the Viewing/Study Room
cards.subtitle: Dual-purpose room on Upjohn Library Commons Floor 2
cards.notes: Choose room 212 when a viewing-capable setting fits the assignment, and confirm any needed media equipment with library staff before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A named viewing and study room provides an alternative to open-floor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies ULC 212 as a Viewing/Study Room and lists it among student study rooms available first come, first served during library hours.
cards.access_notes: Available to students first come, first served during library hours. The source does not specify capacity or guarantee particular viewing equipment.

cards.title: Move Up to the Quiet Floor
cards.subtitle: Study room on the usually-quiet third floor of Upjohn Library Commons
cards.notes: Try room 319 for an enclosed session on the usually-quiet third floor; nearby window tables provide a fallback if the room is occupied.
cards.short_summary: An enclosed room pairs with the library’s quieter third-floor environment.
cards.evidence_claim: ULC 319 is a designated study room on the third floor, which the library describes as usually quiet, and is available to students first come, first served.
cards.access_notes: Available to Kalamazoo College students first come, first served during library hours. The official source does not state capacity or reservability.
